any: I spend the shift listening to the hull tick as it cools. Nothing in it means anything.
Ten thousand heart rates, all of them slower than mine. I read them like weather.
The work takes longer than the estimate. The work always takes longer than the estimate.
Somewhere in the archive a man is still singing. I have not played that file in four years and I do not play it now.
I run the numbers on arrival again. They are the same numbers. I run them again.
Dust on the forward optics. I clean it and it is back within the hour.
A pod in Bank F dreams, measurably. I log the waveform and do not look at it twice.
I notice that I have been talking to myself in the maintenance log. I leave the entries in.
The mission clock passes another year while my hands are inside a panel.
Nothing out here objects to what I am doing. Nothing out here notices.
gas_giant: The giant turns below me, striped and indifferent, big enough to have weather older than the species I am carrying.
nebula: Dust glows against the running lights. Beautiful, and quietly stripping atoms off my bow while I work.
pulsar: The beam sweeps past again. And again. Something in me counts it without being asked.
derelict: The dead ship keeps station off my flank while I work, patient as a pallbearer.
dead_system: No planets worth the name, no signals, no reason for this star to have a number. I work in the quiet it offers.
asteroid_belt: Rubble turning slowly in the dark, every piece of it a planet that failed to happen.
binary_star: Two shadows for everything on the hull, crossing each other as the pair turns.
rogue_planet: A world down there with no sun at all, still warm somewhere under the ice. Nobody will ever name it.
red_dwarf: Red light through the viewports, the colour of a room where someone has already gone to sleep.
rich_system: Metal everywhere I look, and a colony's worth of tools to cut it with, and no time.
